subject: API dependency map & success path — next steps for Open model migration
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Turner <samuel.turner@acmelabs.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: API dependency map & success path — next steps for Open model migration

Hi Sam / Leah —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our conversation and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Key pain points you shared
- Vendor lock-in: heavy reliance on proprietary API semantics (OpenAI function-calling + Anthropic chat formats) that make safe cutover brittle.
- Cost: ~8M tokens/month across gen + embeddings; current spend has been trending up with peak bursts.
- Latency & forecasting: p95 spikes during batch processing affecting UX and burst auto-scaling is unpredictable.
- Compliance: need for residency and audit logs (SOC2 + more granular access logs).

Current stack you described
- Primary generation: OpenAI API (chat completions + function-calling) for user-facing assistants.
- Safety/guardrails: in-house filter layer + Anthropic for higher-safety flows.
- Embeddings: mixed (OpenAI + small self-hosted vector service).
- Orchestration: internal gateway that normalizes inputs/outputs and routes per use case.

Compatibility & must-haves for migration
- Protocol compatibility: function-calling equivalents or a lightweight adapter layer.
- Streaming support: token-by-token streaming for interactive UI.
- Role-based context & KV cache preservation for multi-turn chats.
- Embedding shape parity (dimension + normalization) or migration plan for vector rebuild.
- SSO + KMS for key management and audit trails.

Success criteria (internal + product)
- Latency: match or improve current p95 for 1–2k concurrent chat sessions (<150ms server-side target for cached prefixes).
- Cost: demonstrable <3x of current per-token unit economics in PoC with realistic traffic profile.
- Feature parity: function-calling, streaming, and conversational context retained with <10% deviation in end-user task success metrics on sample prompts.
- Compliance: SOC2 evidence and regionally isolated deployment for PII flows.

Suggested next steps
1) Technical deep-dive (90m) with your infra + platform engineers — target week of Jun 28.
2) PoC scope doc: 2-week PoC focusing on chat assistant (function-calling + embeddings) — we provide a baseline config and sample load profile.
3) Provide compatibility matrix (attached) and our recommended adapter patterns for function-calling.
4) Exchange SOC2 summary and network topology requirements — we’ll start a PLA (preliminary architecture) doc.

Attachments: propapi-dep-map-v1.pdf (dependency map we sketched during call), technical-compatibility-matrix.xlsx (compatibility checklist + model feature matrix).

If the above looks right, can you confirm which engineers we should include for the tech deep-dive and whether you prefer Wed/Thu next week?

Thanks,
Rachel

Rachel Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0162

Subject: Re: API dependency map & success path — next steps for Open model migration

Thanks Rachel — this is a great summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Token volumes: the 8M tokens/month is a blended figure. For generation alone it's closer to 6.2M, embeddings ~1.6M. We can share a traffic slice and a sample prompt set for the PoC.
2) Function-calling: our gateway currently uses the OpenAI function schema. We need to preserve the typed JSON outputs; losing structure during adapter translation is a non-starter.
3) Privacy: for our EU customers we’ll need a regionally isolated deployment for storing conversation history.

Engineers to join the deep-dive:
- Leah Chen (platform lead) — leah.chen@acmelabs.com
- Marco Ruiz (infra lead) — marco.ruiz@acmelabs.com (cc in follow-up)

Wed or Thu both work; prefer Wed morning (PST). Please send a calendar invite.

Sam

Appreciate the clarifications, Sam — that aligns with what we'll use for the PoC. Two quick items I added:

- PoC scope: 2-week pilot targeting the main chat flow (generation + function-calling + embeddings for intent matching). We’ll provide an adapter shim that preserves the OpenAI-style function schema so your gateway sees minimal changes.
- Data residency: we can propose a dedicated VPC/private deployment for EU historic data flows — engineering will outline the network and KMS options in the deep-dive.

I’ve scheduled the technical deep-dive for Wed Jul 7, 2026 at 09:30 PST — calendar invite sent to the list (please accept). Agenda attached in the invite; primary asks for your team: sample prompt set, traffic profile export, and a redaction policy for PII.

Next internal steps for us at Redwood: Marissa and Rishi will build the PoC config (traffic replay + adapter), and I’ll assemble SOC2 + architecture artifacts.

Best,
Rachel

Rachel Kim
